parsed.explanation: No dossier was supplied, so this rests on general knowledge, which I held with moderate confidence. Nepal has no trans-specific criminal offence and no enforcement of anti-trans or sodomy law. Its 2007 Supreme Court ruling protects gender identity and recognises a third gender, and the 2015 constitution recognises gender and sexual minorities. Nepal also issues third-gender 'O' passports. These are resident-facing machinery and so count as climate signals only. The cultural record shows an established hijra/third-gender presence and relative social tolerance, with no documented state targeting of visitors. Gaps remain. Rural conservatism, family-level hostility and discrimination against local trans people are local-sphere issues that do not demonstrably reach visitors. Open questions include how foreign documents with a mismatched marker are treated, and facilities and custody practice, which I could not verify. Overall: reduced risk, near the top of that band.
